Mr. Gupta apprised the Court of the facilities available at their institution. He began by stating that the facility fosters a strong sense of community, where approximately 30 to 35 children and individuals with special needs are supported by a staff trained to address their specific requirements. He further Vinod Kumar Poddar & Anr vs Local Level Committee Through Dc South ... on 3 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/72096421/ 1 explained that the management ensures the well-being of residents by adhering to all necessary regulations concerning food safety and other standards. The institution has an on-site medical facility, and a hospital is located just five minutes away. Mr. Gupta added that, rather than providing formal education, they focus on skilling individuals through vocational training. Moreover, music, sports, and other activities form an integral part of the daily routine set for the residents. 2. In response to the Court's query, Mr. Gupta submits that the facility requires approximately three to four days to assess the special needs of any individual intending to reside there. 5. Counsel for Respondent No.1 submits that they have no objection to the request made in this application.
texts.arguments: He has offered to take Mr. Rohan Podar under the care of the foundation, assuring the Court that this option would be in the best interest of Mr. Rohan Podar. 3. Mr. A. K. Chauhan, counsel for Respondent No.3 and the intervenor, strongly opposes the application. He submits that Mr. Rohan Podar has lived in the house, set up by his father for a long period of time and relocating him would be catastrophic for Mr. Rohan Podar's well-being. He also draws the attention of this Court to Section 10 of the National Trust for the Welfare of Persons with Autism, Cerebral Palsy, Mental Retardation, and Multiple Disabilities Act, 1999.
